newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot security at international level-official.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot security at international level-official.

text.p: Russia's flagship carrier Aeroflot has achieved international standards of air security, a senior International Air Transport Association (IATA) official said on Monday.
Brian Wall, IATA's director of security services, spoke in Moscow, where he was meeting Aeroflot officials on air security measures.
"We consider that Aeroflot's air security measures correspond to international standards," he told a press conference.
Aeroflot's acting chief executive Valery Okulov told reporters that his company had invested 12 billion roubles ($2 million) to improve its air security.
"We will study IATA's air security measures and try to spread its recommendations to other Russian air carriers," Okulov said.

He said that all passenger baggage on Aeroflot's internal and international flights are inspected before takeoff. Aeroflot's air security service also recently set up an anti-terrorist department equipped to detect explosives.
The head of Aeroflot's security service Vladimir Antonov said last year there was only one hijack attempt during the year, which did not result in any injuries.
In that incident, a hijacker with a knife threatened passengers on a flight from Moscow to Nigeria before he was arrested on board by Aeroflot's security representatives, he said.
But many Russian passengers still try to travel with weapons, officials say.
Russia's Federal Aviation Service said officials confiscated about 44,000 arms at airports from passengers, compared with 63,000 in 1995.
